one_line: Seller-controlled authority layer for agentic commerce.
what_it_does: Lets sellers define mandates for quantity, value, discount, and stock, then pauses out-of-policy orders for explicit approval before commit and receipt creation.
leverage_rationale: Structured, role-scoped tools and server-side mandate enforcement materially change agent reliability and safety; a general UI-driving agent could not safely reproduce the authority boundary as precisely.
leverage_evidence: Description specifies APPROVAL_REQUIRED for six RAM modules against a five-item mandate.
commit_action is available only after visible human approval, with versioned mandates, atomic transactions, and idempotency checks.
Frame evidence shows a seller portal and order decision queue.
execution_rationale: The claimed workflow is coherent and unusually complete for a synthetic commerce demo, but there is no submitted video and end-to-end operation is described rather than demonstrated.
execution_evidence: Claims buyer and seller portals, seven tools, persistent orders/inventory/approvals/receipts, and 65 regression tests.
Frame sheet shows seller-portal order review states and decision controls.
impact_rationale: It addresses a concrete trust and authorization problem in agentic commerce, with useful seller control even though the demo has no real payments or customer validation.
impact_evidence: Explicitly targets enforceable spending, inventory, discount, approval, and audit boundaries.
creativity_rationale: The seller-controlled mandate and auditable exception-approval model is a fresh, well-targeted interaction pattern for agentic commerce.
creativity_evidence: Numerical mandate plus pending exception and approval receipt are central to the concept.
usability_note: Portal flow appears understandable; approval workflow may be operationally clear, but evidence is limited.
red_flags: No submitted video; all implementation and test claims are self-reported.
Synthetic data and no real payment/shipment.
standouts: Human approval is enforced as a server authority boundary, not merely a UI convention.
advance_reason: Strong WebMCP-specific safety leverage and concrete commerce use case.

one_line: WebMCP Gmail manager operating inside the user's authenticated browser session.
what_it_does: Loads inbox messages, retrieves details, marks messages read, and sends threaded replies through WebMCP tools without sharing API keys with a third party.
leverage_rationale: Running in the user's authenticated session and exposing typed email/thread operations improves trust and precision, though a capable general agent can perform much of the same UI workflow.
leverage_evidence: Claims tools execute inside the user's authenticated Gmail session with no third-party API key.
Devpost screenshot visibly shows Gmail-like UI and WebMCP-related console operations.
Frame evidence shows load, message detail, reply, and send states.
execution_rationale: The core inbox-to-reply flow is visibly represented, but several frames are low resolution and the packet lacks a video, so completeness and live success are only partially evidenced.
execution_evidence: Frames show inbox loading, email detail, reply field, and Send reply control.
Description names FastAPI, PostgreSQL, Google sign-in, and threaded reply headers.
impact_rationale: Email is a high-frequency personal workflow and the session-local trust boundary is a credible benefit for users who want agent assistance without surrendering credentials.
impact_evidence: Clear audience: Gmail users needing reading, organization, and replies.
Explicitly addresses API-key sharing and closed-chatbot trust concerns.
creativity_rationale: A solid WebMCP application of a familiar email manager, with a meaningful security/session angle but limited conceptual novelty.
creativity_evidence: All core email actions are registered as discoverable page tools.
usability_note: The visible inbox and reply flow is conventional and legible, though sign-in and loading add friction.
red_flags: No video; frame text is partly illegible.
Live Gmail behavior and authorization boundaries are claimed more strongly than independently evidenced.
standouts: Correct-thread reply handling and user-session trust boundary.
Visible developer-tool evidence of WebMCP operations.
advance_reason: Credible, useful WebMCP integration with visible core workflow.

one_line: Human-and-agent invoice reconciliation dashboard with shared row-level context.
what_it_does: Matches messy cross-border deposits to invoices, surfaces receivables, lets agents navigate and highlight exact rows, and drafts chaser letters for human review.
leverage_rationale: Shared structured state plus agent-driven tab switching and row highlighting creates a meaningful human-agent collaboration delta beyond chat or generic screen automation.
leverage_evidence: Eight tools read embedded structured data, switch tabs, flash exact rows, and open drafts.
Nothing is sent automatically; human reviews the draft.
Packet claims live agent call and same-dashboard human visibility.
execution_rationale: The static dashboard and described reconciliation model are coherent and scoped, with visible gallery media and a live demo, though no video limits end-to-end proof.
execution_evidence: Public repository and live demo are listed alive.
Description specifies handling hidden fees, batched and split payments and embedded JSON data.
Gallery evidence is present.
impact_rationale: It targets a real costly operations problem for businesses handling international invoices and gives a concrete, reviewable workflow.
impact_evidence: Specific Thai agri-exporter scenario with wrong amounts and opaque references.
Unpaid surfacing, learned buyer behavior, and draft chasers address recurring reconciliation work.
creativity_rationale: The distinctive idea is not reconciliation alone but an agent pointing to the exact shared dashboard row while proposing a reviewed action.
creativity_evidence: Agent-to-human spatial grounding via tab switching and row flashing is central.
usability_note: Pointing at the same row and requiring review should reduce ambiguity in a dense finance workflow.
red_flags: Core dashboard predates the challenge; WebMCP contribution is narrower than whole product.
Static embedded data limits production realism.
standouts: Human review is preserved for outbound correspondence.
advance_reason: Concrete business value and a clear, demonstrable WebMCP collaboration delta.

one_line: Agent-native vehicle configurator, digital twin, owner guide, and 3D creation engine.
what_it_does: Lets agents inspect and revise a fictional car build, calculate ownership outcomes, control a shared 3D garage, reveal components, and inspect the measurement-driven model workflow.
leverage_rationale: Structured tools across five synchronized 3D contexts enable precise inspection, revision, measurement, and undoable shared state that is difficult to reproduce reliably through UI driving.
leverage_evidence: Claims 49 tools across landing, configurator, Garage, Owner's Guide, and Creation Engine.
Mutations are revision-gated and undoable; results state source or measurement basis.
Public repository and live demo are listed alive.
execution_rationale: The scope is ambitious but internally coherent, and the public repo/live demo plus described tests support a strong claimed execution score; absence of video lowers confidence.
execution_evidence: TypeScript/React/Three.js stack with Vitest and Playwright.
Detailed five-context architecture and 42 named components are claimed.
Fictional reconstruction is explicitly scoped and sourced from public dimensions/photos.
impact_rationale: It offers credible value for car shoppers, owners, and learners needing understandable configuration and vehicle knowledge, though the fictional product narrows immediate practical impact.
impact_evidence: Combines configurator, synchronized digital twin, visual guide, and creation workflow.
Measurement/source basis is exposed to users.
creativity_rationale: This is an unusually deep synthesis of agent control, 3D configuration, digital-twin interaction, and inspectable model creation.
creativity_evidence: Five page contexts and shared 3D vehicle interaction are pursued as one coherent concept.
42 named components and measurement-driven provenance add depth.
usability_note: Many contexts and tools could create complexity, but undo and human interruption are good safeguards.
red_flags: Very broad scope is primarily claimed rather than video-demonstrated.
Fictional vehicle, not manufacturer CAD.
standouts: Revision gating, interruption, undo, and measurement provenance.
advance_reason: Exceptional creativity and substantial structured-agent ambition.

one_line: A live building model that trains operators through conversational agent access.
what_it_does: Extends a building's 3D model into operations and training so technicians, firefighters, and contractors can ask an agent about the live model rather than learn a BIM viewer.
leverage_rationale: For non-experts operating a complex building model, structured agent access can convert a difficult BIM interface into a shared conversational training and operations surface.
leverage_evidence: Description explicitly targets week-two technicians, firefighters, and contractors.
Claims WebMCP reaches into the live model on screen rather than stale exports.
execution_rationale: The concept and narrative are strong, but no video frame sheets were submitted and the packet provides no concrete end-to-end workflow evidence, so execution is capped.
execution_evidence: Five Devpost gallery images are listed, but no frame sheets were submitted.
Description articulates operations/training intent but not a demonstrated completed interaction.

impact_evidence: Specific audiences include technicians, firefighters, and isolation contractors.
Clear argument that models otherwise stop being useful at handover.
creativity_rationale: Repurposing BIM from design artifact into a conversational operational training layer is a memorable and ambitious concept.
creativity_evidence: The model is positioned as a long-lived operational and training interface, not merely a viewer.
usability_note: Conversational access could aid non-experts, but no visible product flow is available to assess.
red_flags: No submitted video frame sheets.
Core implementation and agent interaction are not evidenced in the packet.
standouts: High-value emergency and training use case.
advance_reason: Impact and concept are compelling, but evidence is too thin for a blind Stage 1 advance.

one_line: Collaborative time-based financial scenario builder controlled by users and agents.
what_it_does: Creates cards for salaries, interest, debt, expenses, and inflation, then visualizes calculations over dates from milliseconds to years with WebMCP agent control.
leverage_rationale: Structured scenario creation and manipulation can make complex repeated calculations more repeatable than UI automation, but the underlying graph/calculator outcome remains attainable with general agents.
leverage_evidence: Description says agents can create models and control scenarios alongside users.
Frame sheets reportedly show ChatGPT in-app browser views of the product.
execution_rationale: The concept, cards, timelines, and visualization are coherent, with live demo and gallery evidence, but the packet lacks a video and the detailed end-to-end behavior is only partially visible.
execution_evidence: Live demo is listed alive and four gallery images are present.
Description identifies recurring financial operations and date-range modeling.
impact_rationale: Domestic budgeting and scenario planning are real needs, and visualizing timing effects can help users understand otherwise abstract arithmetic.
impact_evidence: Specific use cases include salaries, recurring interest, inflation, debt payments, and expenses.
Goal is simplifying financial representations across cultures.
creativity_rationale: The combination of graph-like cards, real-life time progression, and shared agent/user scenario editing is a fresh synthesis.
creativity_evidence: Supports unusually fine-grained time representations from milliseconds to years.
Agent and user operate on the same scenario model.
usability_note: Cards and visual timelines may clarify scenarios, but financial setup could be demanding.
red_flags: No video; numeric correctness and tool execution are not independently demonstrated.
Scope and audience are broad.
standouts: Time-aware visualization gives familiar financial calculations a tangible form.
advance_reason: Clear product concept with meaningful collaborative agent use and credible niche impact.

impact_evidence: Clear game audience and stated future applications to RPGs, tactics, simulators, and survival games.

one_line: Local-first contract verification gate with source-grounded, approval-controlled terms.
what_it_does: Extracts contract terms, links each to exact source text, stages proposed changes, requires human approval before saving, and exports an audit trail.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP's staged write-lock and explicit approval model creates reliable shared human-agent state for a high-risk document workflow; generic UI control is less trustworthy.

Local browser processing preserves document boundary.

execution_evidence: Public repository and live demo are listed alive.

impact_evidence: Targets auto-renewals, notice periods, and liability limits.

creativity_rationale: The combination of source-grounded extraction, local-first privacy, and an approval gate is a thoughtful and memorable legal-AI interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Browser-native verification gate and write-lock are central rather than cosmetic features.
usability_note: Quote links and confidence cues support review; legal users may still need domain expertise.

standouts: Local-first handling is well matched to sensitive contracts.

one_line: Studio for discovering website capabilities and composing them into WebMCP tools.
what_it_does: Scans semantic DOM/forms/actions, records evidence and effects, lets developers compose workflows, and generates higher-level tools for controlled live-page interaction.
leverage_rationale: The product directly creates the structured agent surface missing from ordinary sites, with capability graphs, schemas, validated bindings, and workflow composition; this is not merely a UI convenience.
leverage_evidence: Discovery covers semantic HTML, forms, controls, Shadow DOM, and same-origin frames.
Capability graph stores schemas, locators, evidence, confidence, and effects.
Generated tools register through document.modelContext and compose primitives into buy_best_product-style workflows.
execution_rationale: Architecture and judge path are unusually well specified, with hosted Studio and optional MV3 extension, but no video means central discovery-to-execution completion is only claimed.
execution_evidence: Packet describes hosted Studio, controlled commerce/travel targets, bridge, interpreter, and extension.
Specific workflow searches, filters, views details, and adds to cart.
Frame sheets are submitted.
impact_rationale: It addresses the ecosystem-level bottleneck that most existing sites are not agent-ready, offering developers a plausible migration and workflow-composition path.
impact_evidence: Clear developer audience and explicit problem of production websites lacking agent-native capabilities.
Reviewable evidence/confidence/effects can improve maintainability and safety.
creativity_rationale: Inferring capabilities from semantic surfaces and compiling them into reusable, higher-level WebMCP tools is an original and ambitious infrastructure concept.
creativity_evidence: Combines discovery, evidence graph, validated interpreter, and tool generation in one product.
usability_note: Drag-and-drop workflow composition is approachable, though discovery confidence and extension eligibility may complicate use.
red_flags: Hosted flow limits external URLs to potential-only; live instrumentation requires optional extension.
No video; claims of broad discovery are not independently observed.
standouts: Evidence/effects/confidence model is a notable safety and debugging feature.
advance_reason: High leverage and ecosystem relevance, with a concrete composition workflow.
